newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank down on central bank inspired lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank down on central bank inspired lending.

text.p: Interbank rates eased across the board as some big local banks, who are also agents for Bank Negara, continued lending one-month money, dealers said on Wednesday.
By 0345 GMT, one-month money had slipped to 8.0 percent from 8.5 at the open, three-month fell to 7.8/8.1 percent from 8.3 and six-month to 7.5 percent from 8.0/3.
One-week money was being lent at 8.2 percent against 8.7 at the open.
"It looks like Bank Negara is still injecting funds into the market," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said lending by two of the big banks of the country had capped one-month money at the current level.
Dealers said there was more downside to interest rates over the next few days as the central bank injects more funds.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past week to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly higher to reflect the fall in interbank rates.
At 0345 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up three at 92.42, or an implied yield of 7.58 percent.
The December contract was up four at 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
